Votes

How the counted ballots voted — from the counties’ cast-vote records (CVR). Filter by geography (pick a district type, then a district or county), by the party the voter chose (partisan vote choice), by the contest that choice was made in — U.S. House, State Senate, or State House — and by how the voter voted on Amendment B, and see how those same ballots voted in each contest and on Amendment B. The partisan and Amendment B filters combine: pick a party choice and a Yes/No on Amendment B to see just those ballots. CVR data as of Wed Nov 18, 2026, 7:44 PM MST.
Partial data. Partial: 28 of 29 counties merged (1,053,628 ballots); complete after the Nov 23 canvass. Figures on this page come from CVR files only — they are not final statewide totals. Counties included (28 of 29): Beaver, Box Elder, Cache, Carbon, Daggett, Davis, Duchesne, Emery, Garfield, Grand, Iron, Juab, Kane, Millard, Morgan, Piute, Rich, Salt Lake, Sanpete, Sevier, Summit, Tooele, Uintah, Utah, Wasatch, Washington, Wayne, Weber.

How these ballots voted — by contest

Each bar stacks only votes cast in that contest, as a share of all ballots in the filter — so a shorter bar means more undervotes. Segment labels are the share of votes cast in that contest (undervotes and overvotes excluded from the denominator); hover a segment for the raw ballot count and that contest’s undervotes. The number above each bar is the votes cast in that contest — the sum of the bar’s segments. For SD, only ballots with an SD contest on the ballot are in the bar (SD seats are staggered — only 15 were on the 2026 ballot). The HD and Amendment B bars likewise exclude federal-only ballots, which carry no HD contest and no Amendment B value.

Sources & method. Cast-vote records published by the counties (Disclosure Controlled CVR files) via the state results site; 1,053,628 ballot rows from 28 counties. “Other” in the partisan vote choice filter is third-party and independent votes in the chosen contest; ballots with no vote in that contest (undervotes) appear only under “Any party”. The Amendment B filter works the same way: ballots that undervoted on Amendment B appear only under “Any”. Registration and official turnout are the tracker’s figures (active registered voters, Nov 3 voted file; turnout = ballots counted ÷ active registered). County registration and turnout use total registered voters (Nov 2026). All figures are unofficial until canvassed. Source CVR master: utah-statewide-cvr-2026.csv (1,053,628 ballots, 28 counties merged). Candidate->party mapping from All-Results_2026-11-18_1209-MST.xlsx (Summary Results sheet, authoritative); 2,583,370 candidate cells mapped via Excel, 0 via CVR party-prefix fallback, 0 unmapped. Registration denominator: active registered voters (Nov 2026) from the State Dashboard; statewide 1,784,255 = sum of county Total registered (Nov 3 voted file). Turnout = ballots in results / registered, the tracker's definition. County registration and turnout use TOTAL registered voters (Nov 2026), not active. Per-district turnout ballots = 'Ballots Cast' for that office in the Summary Results sheet of the same All Results file; district-stats.json does not carry ballots counted per district (only candidate vote totals). Amendment B values in the CVR are FOR/AGAINST (family A, Weber title-case, Rich with candidate-ID suffixes), mapped to Yes/No; YES/NO would be accepted too. AmB 'total' = ballots with a non-blank AmB value; 793 ballots have a blank AmB (federal-only ballots, see below) and are excluded from the AmB total so Yes+No+undervotes+overvotes reconciles to total. 793 ballots have a CD contest but no HD contest, no SD contest, and blank Amendments A/B (federal-only ballots: a CD vote and nothing else on the ballot). They count in 'All' groups, in no HD/SD geography, and in the HD/SD no-contest counts. Partisan vote choice groups: R/D/Other = ballots whose choice in the defining contest (U.S. House, State Senate, or State House) was that party; undervotes and overvotes in the defining contest, and ballots with no such contest on the ballot, are in 'All' only. Write-ins count as Other and are also reported separately under 'writeins'. Overvotes count as neither a vote nor an undervote. Amendment B filter groups: Yes/No = ballots that voted Yes/No on Amendment B; AmB undervotes, overvotes, and ballots with a blank AmB value are in 'All' only. The partisan and Amendment B filters combine independently — e.g. the CD/R/Yes group is the ballots that voted Republican in the U.S. House contest AND Yes on Amendment B; with partisan choice 'Any', the AmB groups show how Yes/No-on-B voters voted in each contest regardless of party choice. Overvotes in tabulated contests (CD/SD/HD/AmB): 0. Write-ins in tabulated contests: 1902 (file-wide write-ins in local contests are not counted here). Millard County's CVR was posted as a PDF (an Excel print-to-PDF, 1,045 content pages in 11 column blocks); it was reconstructed by coordinate extraction and validated contest-by-contest against the official Millard results before merging.
Sources: Utah Lieutenant Governor’s election results (electionresults.utah.gov) — state All-Results reports and county Ballot Statistics reports; county clerk reconciliation pages; the State Dashboard (November 2026) for registration. District boundaries: Utah Geospatial Resource Center (AGRC). All figures are unofficial until canvassed. This tracker is not affiliated with the State of Utah or any county.
